question.problem:
The marginal CDFs of two continuous independent random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below. 

$$
{F}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0 \\ \frac{1}{4}{x}^{2}, & 0\le x\le 2 \\ 1, & x>2\end{aligned}\,\,{F}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & y<0 \\ \frac{1}{8}{y}^{3}, & 0\le y\le 2 \\ 1, & y>2\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expression for the joint CDF when $0\le x\le 2$ and $0\le y\le 2.$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are independent continuous random variables with marginal CDFs ${F}_{X}(x)$ and ${F}_{Y}(y),$ respectively, then the corresponding joint CDF of $F(x,y)$ is given by

$$
F(x,y)={F}_{X}(x)\cdot {F}_{Y}(y).
$$

Therefore, for $0\le x\le 2$ and $0\le y\le 2,$ the joint CDF for our random variables is 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y) & ={F}_{X}(x)\cdot {F}_{Y}(y) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{8}{y}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{32}{x}^{2}{y}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for the joint CDF is

$$
F(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0\text{ or }y<0 \\ \frac{1}{32}{x}^{2}{y}^{3}, & 0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 2 \\ \frac{1}{4}{x}^{2}, & 0\le x\le 2,\,y>2 \\ \frac{1}{8}{y}^{3}, & x>2,\,0\le y\le 2 \\ 1, & x>2,\,y>2\end{aligned}
$$
